name: Stress Recovery Theory
citation: Ulrich, R.S. (1983). Aesthetic and affective response to natural environment. In I. Altman & J.F. Wohlwill (Eds.), Behavior and the natural environment (pp. 85-125). Plenum.

constructs.description: Rapid (100ms-5s) positive affective shift via pulvinar low road. Five-stage subcortical cascade: retina → SC → pulvinar → amygdala → hypothalamus → autonomic initiation.
Ventral vagal dominance (not dorsal vagal). vmPFC tonic sympathetic inhibition when amygdala threat detection is low. Measured by RSA, not generic HRV.
HPA axis downregulation — nature prevents new cortisol release and allows existing cortisol to clear (half-life 60-90 min). Sapolsky's virtuous cycle: recovery enables more recovery.

schema_gaps: Enteric vagal pathway (rest-and-digest) not yet templated
irreducible_residual.narrative: Minimal residual for mechanism. The residual concerns the subjective quality of the affective shift — why a safety signal 'feels good' rather than merely reducing arousal. This phenomenological dimension is partially addressable through interoceptive inference (IC framework) but remains a classic hard-problem frontier. The implicit-automatic processing channel — the claim that stress recovery begins before conscious evaluation — is the core organizing principle.

key_references: Ulrich, R.S. (1984). View through a window. Science, 224(4647), 420-421.
Ulrich, R.S. et al. (1991). Stress recovery during exposure. J. Environ. Psychol., 11(3), 201-230.
Porges, S.W. (2011). The polyvagal theory. Norton.

boundary_criteria.boundary_justification: SRT claims an affective response pattern (rapid positive shift → autonomic recovery) that is not fully T1-decomposable (compositional_adequacy = INTERACTION_DEPENDENT). Autonomic recovery (parasympathetic activation, HPA downregulation) is constitutively relevant to stress reduction — intervening on recovery mechanisms directly changes the outcome. Design guidance is specific: vegetation type, water visibility, spatial openness all produce measurable recovery curves distinct from other T1 predictions.

provenance.seminal_paper: Ulrich, R.S. (1983). Aesthetic and affective response to natural environment. In Behavior and the Natural Environment.
provenance.predecessor: Zajonc's affective primacy hypothesis; evolutionary aesthetics (Appleton, 1975)
provenance.historical_context: Proposed that nature triggers automatic positive affective responses that reduce stress. The 1984 hospital study (view through window) became one of the most cited papers in environmental psychology.
